intro.heading: Contracts change the money, not the structure.
intro.body: Your entry can be clean and your stop loss can be correct, but if your size is too big, the trade becomes emotionally heavy. Position sizing is what makes the same setup feel manageable or reckless — the chart doesn't care how many contracts you're in, but you will.
intro.dayliNote: Keep your size consistent. Going heavier because confidence is high, or doubling size after a loss, is emotion talking — not a risk plan.

chart.heading: Same setup, two different sizes
chart.prompt: Tap each size to see how the same 10-point stop changes weight.

left.label: 1 contract
left.desc: 1 MNQ contract on a 10-point stop risks $20. Small, manageable, easy to think clearly through.

right.label: 10 contracts
right.desc: 10 MNQ contracts on the exact same 10-point stop risks $200 — the setup didn't change, the weight did.

tapCards.prompt: Two traders take the identical setup — same entry, same stop, same target — but one uses 1 contract and the other uses 10. Is one trade objectively better structured?

options.label: No — the structure is identical; only the dollar risk and emotional weight differ
options.feedback: Right — sizing changes the weight of the trade, not its quality.

options.label: Yes — more contracts always means a better trade
options.feedback: More contracts doesn't make a setup better — it only makes it bigger.

tapCards.prompt: You just had two wins in a row and feel great. Do you increase your size because confidence is high?

options.label: No — size should come from your risk plan, not your mood
options.feedback: Right — confidence isn't a risk management input.

options.label: Yes — you've earned bigger size
options.feedback: Sizing up because of a feeling is exactly how good runs turn into big losses.

tapCards.prompt: After a loss, a trader doubles her next position size to "win it back faster." What's actually happening?

options.label: Emotion is driving her sizing decision, not her risk plan
options.feedback: Exactly — that's revenge sizing, and it compounds risk right when discipline matters most.

options.label: That's a smart way to recover losses quickly
options.feedback: Increasing size to chase back a loss usually increases risk at the worst possible moment.

quiz.question: Two traders take the identical setup — same entry, same stop, same target — but one uses 1 contract and the other uses 10. Is one trade objectively better structured than the other?
options: No — the structure is identical; only the dollar risk and emotional weight differ between them
Yes — more contracts always means a better trade
Yes — fewer contracts always means a safer, more valid setup
quiz.explanation: Sizing decides how much is on the line — it doesn't change whether the setup itself is good.

quiz.question: Why can the same chart setup be a smart trade for one trader and a reckless trade for another?
options: Position size determines how much dollar risk and emotional weight is actually attached to it
Because charts are different for every trader
Because only the entry price matters, not the size
quiz.explanation: The same structurally sound setup can be reasonable at a small size and reckless at an oversized one.

quiz.question: Your contract size should be decided by your ___, not by how confident or excited you feel today.
quiz.explanation: A risk plan stays consistent regardless of how a trader feels in the moment.
